dedupe_keys.name: newspace index commercial satellite constellations database

description: NewSpace Index is a database of commercial satellite constellations, active, planned and cancelled, with 489 constellations in its table at reading. Erik Kulu has kept it since 2016, adding constellations one by one as he finds them, and uses it for yearly surveys presented at the International Astronautical Congress and the Small Satellite Conference; sister sites cover nanosatellites and small launchers. Each row gives the organisation, satellites launched against planned, first launch year, form factor, field (for example IoT and M2M, AIS, Earth observation, satellite internet, PNT, SAR, weather) and funding, and the site defines what counts as a constellation (three or more similar spacecraft under shared control). Coverage is global, from 2002 onwards; the table was last updated on 31 July 2026. Format and access: an HTML table on the website plus summary graphs as PDF and SVG, with a changelog. Licence: not stated on the page; free to view. Caveats: planned numbers come from company announcements and many plans are delayed or cancelled. It supports capacity planning of space and telecom infrastructure and scenarios of future orbital congestion. A related catalogue record is Jonathan McDowell's list of large satellite constellations.
